indicators.label: Financially included adults
indicators.definition: Adults using formal and/or informal financial products or services; financially included means served through either channel.
indicators.locator: NISR FinScope Survey (2024) publication summary; opening findings. Reports 96% (7.8 million), up from 93% in 2020.
indicators.limitation: National survey estimate, not a measure of individual cooperative participation, financial resilience, or causal program impact.
indicators.productImplication: Use as national context for financial access; measure Huriza's own synthetic workflows separately and never present them as observed national impact.

indicators.label: Adults saving through a group
indicators.definition: Share of adults saving via a group such as a cooperative, VSLA, tontine, or ikimina. The report's accompanying text describes about 4 million adults (52%) using savings groups; channel use is not exclusive.
indicators.population: Rwandan adults (about 4 million; report text explicitly states 52% of adults)
indicators.locator: Rwanda FinScope Survey 2024 report, printed p. 44, paragraph immediately before Figure 35: savings groups 'about 4 million or 52%' after describing 60% informal savers; Figure 35 on printed p. 45 shows 52% group channel in 2024 (55% in 2020).
indicators.limitation: This describes adults using savings groups, not group membership or participation in any specific product. Saving channels overlap, and group saving does not establish active membership, savings amount, or impact.
indicators.productImplication: Support transparent group records and member-level savings tracking while avoiding a claim that every group saver uses a digital cooperative product.

indicators.label: Adults who own or have used mobile money
indicators.definition: Adults who own a registered mobile money account or have used mobile money, including use of another person's wallet.
indicators.locator: Rwanda FinScope Survey 2024 report, section 3.2 'Mobile money usage', printed page 40; approximately 86% (6.9 million) have used services; Figure 25 distinguishes account ownership from use without own account.
indicators.limitation: Ownership/use is not equivalent to registered personal wallet ownership, active monthly use, reliable connectivity, or consent to transact.
indicators.productImplication: Design for mobile-enabled workflows but preserve assisted and non-digital alternatives; any demo payment must be explicitly synthetic.

indicators.label: Population living in poverty
indicators.definition: EICV7 poverty estimate under the updated poverty measurement methodology.
indicators.population: Rwanda population represented by EICV7 household survey
indicators.locator: EICV7 Main Indicators Report 2023/24 official publication summary; poverty headline reports 27.4% in 2023/24. The same summary says a modeled 2016/17 rate under the updated method is 39.8%.
indicators.limitation: National household-survey estimate under updated methodology; it does not establish poverty status for a specific Huriza user, group, or district or prove intervention impact.
indicators.productImplication: Frame poverty as national context and keep beneficiary outcomes unclaimed unless measured with suitable longitudinal evidence.

sources.title: Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey 7 (EICV7), NISR survey page

methodology: Values are manually transcribed only from the cited official NISR publication pages or reports; no microdata, district allocations, or synthetic records enter these national indicators.
The build script validates each curated record's numeric value, provenance locator, population, definition, limitation, and source URL before producing data/insights.json.
Percentages describe their stated survey population and definition; the 52% group-savings figure is among adults who save and allows multiple channels.
Published national estimates are context only and do not establish Huriza product usage, local need, financial inclusion outcomes, or causal impact.

competition.title: NISR 2026 Big Data Hackathon
competition.track2: Financial Inclusion & Poverty Reduction: use data to understand financial exclusion, poverty dynamics, and social-protection impact; solution must use NISR data, optionally with open/public data related to poverty, household income, or financial access; practical impact for vulnerable households, policymakers, or civil society encouraged.
requirements: Two students per team; at least one Rwandan citizen.
Undergraduate or master's students; student card or other official eligibility proof.
Public GitHub link, deployed app link, and documentation expected.
AI tools may be used but must be disclosed; entrants remain responsible; plagiarism prohibited.
competition.intellectualProperty: The page states entrants agree to assign and transfer all IP rights in submitted work, including copyright and patent, to NISR; NISR reserves rights to use, reproduce, modify, publish, and distribute it for any purpose.
unresolved: The page does not state a timezone for its 11:59 PM deadlines.
No separate webinar/video source was verified; confirm any clarifying guidance directly with NISR.
